assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks turn laser-cooled atoms trapped at the magic wavelength into frequency standards with fractional uncertainty near 1e-18, far beyond the caesium definition of the second. The idea (Doppler- and recoil-free spectroscopy in a lattice where the light shift cancels) is simple and original, and the clocks now test fundamental constants, relativistic redshift over millimetres and possible dark-matter couplings. This is precision atomic physics at its best and measures time inside atoms with extraordinary care.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and first demonstrated it with strontium; Ye's group brought the stability and accuracy to the 1e-18 level and the link to frequency combs. Two laureates is a clean configuration. Others (Lemonde, Ludlow, Kimble and colleagues, and Hall and Hansch already recognised for combs) contributed, but the decisive pair is fairly clear.
assessment.maturity: Many independent laboratories (JILA, RIKEN/Tokyo, SYRTE, PTB, NIST, others) have reproduced and extended the results, and the interpretation is very stable. Timely, with the redefinition of the second under discussion. Little risk of premature recognition.
uncertainties: Whether the committee wants to credit the ion-clock lineage (Wineland, Hall) separately or treat it as already covered.
I rely on my own knowledge of the history of the magic-wavelength proposal and have not verified priority details independently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and the Z2 topological insulator, followed by experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells, opened an entire field of topological band theory with robust edge and surface states. It is a genuinely new organising principle in nature and not a technology push. Importance and lasting influence are very high, reaching well beyond a single material.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the decisive theoretical step (graphene proposal and the Z2 classification); Molenkamp's group delivered the first experimental realisation of the quantum spin Hall state, following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. The BHZ theorists, Fu, Zhang and the ARPES groups on Bi-Sb and Bi2Se3 are not in the supplied credit list, so the three-person configuration leaves real allocation questions.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed in multiple materials by independent groups for more than fifteen years, with stable interpretation. Recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Credit allocation is contested: the BHZ proposal, 3D topological insulator theory and ARPES confirmation lie outside the supplied names.
Condensed matter is outside my own field and I defer to colleagues on the finer priority questions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposal for quantum gates with trapped ions and the subsequent experimental control of ion registers by Blatt's group form a core pillar of quantum information with atoms. The work gives exquisite control of individual quantum systems and entangled states, which is the kind of boundary-of-quantum-and-classical question I care about. The importance is high, although part of the area was already recognised in 2012 with Wineland and Haroche.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller made the key theoretical proposal; Blatt's group provided leading experimental realisations and scaling (entanglement, gates, teleportation). Wineland, already a laureate, and Monroe/Wineland-group gate demonstrations are not in the credit list, so the experimental part of the credit is somewhat incomplete. Cirac and Zoller also appear in other candidates, so overlap needs to be managed.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed by many ion-trap groups and companies, with high-fidelity gates well beyond demonstration level. The interpretation is stable. Recognition is mature, though overlap with the 2012 prize reduces the novelty argument.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 prize and with the atom-based candidates B025 and B044.
Whether the committee would prefer a theory-only prize for Cirac and Zoller.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Berry's geometric phase and the Aharonov-Bohm and Aharonov-Anandan lineage show that quantum evolution carries a global geometric memory, a conceptually new and unexpected insight that unifies phenomena in atoms, molecules, optics and condensed matter (Born-Oppenheimer curvature, polarisation optics, quantum Hall response, topological band invariants). Clarity and lasting influence are exceptional, and it is fundamental in the sense I value.
assessment.attribution: Berry (1984) is the decisive originator of the geometric phase; Aharonov gave the Aharonov-Bohm effect and the non-adiabatic generalisation (with Anandan, who is not in the supplied credit). Two named people can support a fair prize, but Pancharatnam, Aharonov-Bohm (Bohm is deceased) and Anandan are left out, which makes the allocation imperfect.
assessment.maturity: Extensively verified in optics, NMR, neutron interferometry and condensed matter, and interpretation is stable for decades. Maturity is not a concern. The risk is rather that recognition is long delayed and that the Aharonov-Bohm effect has historical priority concerns.
uncertainties: Priority questions (Pancharatnam, Aharonov-Bohm, Anandan) complicate attribution.
Whether the committee views this as a physics discovery or a mathematical framework.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution turns the no-cloning and entanglement properties of quantum states into a cryptographic principle, with security grounded in the laws of physics. The BB84 protocol and Ekert's Bell-inequality-based protocol link foundational questions to practice. It is original and has had lasting influence on quantum information, although it is partly a protocol idea rather than a discovery about nature.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard are the clear originators of BB84; Ekert's 1991 entanglement-based protocol is a distinct, independent contribution. The three-person configuration is natural, though Wiesner's earlier conjugate-coding idea is an unresolved priority issue and he is not in the credit list.
assessment.maturity: Demonstrated over fibre and satellite links by many groups and commercially deployed, but practical security against implementation attacks is still being debated. Mature as an idea and well confirmed, timely given the 2022 prize for entanglement experiments.
uncertainties: Overlap in spirit with the 2022 prize on Bell tests and quantum information.
Wiesner priority and practical security loopholes.
Closer to information science than to physics discovery in the narrow sense.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realise the Hubbard model in a clean, tunable setting, with the superfluid to Mott insulator transition and single-site resolved quantum gas microscopes. It lets us see many-body quantum physics directly, which fits my interest in atomic systems as precision simulators. The impact on many-body physics is large and ongoing.
assessment.attribution: The Jaksch-Zoller theoretical proposal and the experimental Mott transition (Greiner, Mandel, Esslinger, Hansch, Bloch) both matter; Bloch has been the leader of the field and Greiner led the gas microscope and the 2002 experiment. Zoller and Cirac are credited elsewhere in the list (B005, B044), so I restrict this ballot to the experimentalists; Esslinger and Hansch are not in the supplied names, leaving a significant allocation question.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many laboratories with stable interpretation, although the topic has already been partly recognised by the 2001 BEC prize and the quantum-simulation applications are still developing. Mature enough for recognition, but the boundary between discovery and tool is blurry.
uncertainties: Allocation among theory proposers, Greiner, Esslinger, Bloch and Hansch.
Whether quantum simulation is judged as a discovery or a method.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit quantum electrodynamics brings strong light-matter coupling to superconducting circuits and underlies today's superconducting quantum processors and dispersive readout. The idea is original and well understood, and it connects naturally to my own atomic cavity-QED background. However, the 2025 prize recognised superconducting-circuit quantum effects, so a closely adjacent award would be debatable.
assessment.attribution: Blais and colleagues proposed the architecture; Wallraff and Schoelkopf delivered the first strong-coupling demonstrations and subsequent developments. This three-person configuration is reasonable, though Devoret and Yale colleagues (Girvin, Majer) have important contributions not in the credit list.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed in many laboratories and industry; the physics is stable. Timing is open because of the 2025 prize.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2025 prize may argue for waiting.
Role of Girvin, Devoret and others in the original concepts.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Strongly interacting Fermi gases and the BEC-BCS crossover give a clean, tunable laboratory for pairing and superfluidity, including observation of vortices and the universal thermodynamics near unitarity. It addresses a fundamental many-body question with quantitative agreement between theory and experiment, which I value. It is, however, a refinement of earlier recognised ultracold-gas work.
assessment.attribution: Several leading groups (Grimm, Zwierlein, Salomon, Thomas, Jin, Ketterle) contributed to the molecular BEC and crossover observations. Deborah Jin, a key pioneer, is deceased and not on the credited list, and the list of four names exceeds the three-person limit, so a fair prize would be difficult.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced independently and in good agreement with theory, so maturity is high, but the impact is narrower than the other candidates and the credit problem is serious.
uncertainties: Absence of Jin and the number of leading groups make a fair three-person allocation hard.
Possible redundancy with previous cold-atom prizes.
